name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q01 - Hybridisation and geometry of carbon species

questiontext.text:
Match the carbon-containing species in List I with the correct hybridisation state of carbon and molecular shape in List II:

List I (Species)List II (Hybridisation & Shape)
A. \(\mathrm{CH}_4\)(i) \(sp^2\), trigonal planar
B. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)(ii) \(sp^3\), pyramidal (distorted tetrahedron)
C. \(\mathrm{HC}\equiv\mathrm{N}\)(iii) \(sp^3\), tetrahedral
D. \(\mathrm{CH}_3^-\)(iv) \(sp\), linear

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The hybridisation state and geometry of a carbon atom depend on the number of \(\sigma\)-bonds and lone pairs associated with it: four electron domains correspond to \(sp^3\), three to \(sp^2\), and two to \(sp\) hybridisation.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
In methane (\(\mathrm{CH}_4\)), carbon forms four \(\sigma\)-bonds with zero lone pairs, giving \(sp^3\) hybridisation and tetrahedral shape, matching (iii). In formaldehyde (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)), carbon forms three \(\sigma\)-bonds and one \(\pi\)-bond, giving \(sp^2\) hybridisation and trigonal planar shape, matching (i). In hydrogen cyanide (\(\mathrm{HC}\equiv\mathrm{N}\)), carbon forms two \(\sigma\)-bonds and two \(\pi\)-bonds, giving \(sp\) hybridisation and linear shape, matching (iv). In methyl carbanion (\(\mathrm{CH}_3^-\)), carbon has three \(\sigma\)-bonds and one lone pair, giving \(sp^3\) hybridisation and a pyramidal (distorted tetrahedral) shape, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Combining the matched pairs gives A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q02 - Trivial names and formulas of organic compounds

questiontext.text:
Match the common (trivial) names in List I with their corresponding chemical formulas in List II:

List I (Common Name)List II (Formula)
A. Anisole(i) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCH}_3\)
B. Aniline(ii) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OCH}_3\)
C. Acetophenone(iii) \((\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{C})_4\mathrm{C}\)
D. Neopentane(iv) \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}_2\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Trivial or traditional names are widely retained in organic chemistry for common aromatic derivatives and branched alkanes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
Anisole is methoxybenzene, having the formula \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OCH}_3\), which matches (ii). Aniline is aminobenzene, having the formula \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}_2\), which matches (iv). Acetophenone is methyl phenyl ketone, having the formula \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COCH}_3\), which matches (i). Neopentane is 2,2-dimethylpropane, having a central quaternary carbon bonded to four methyl groups, \((\mathrm{H}_3\mathrm{C})_4\mathrm{C}\), which matches (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match the functional groups in List I with their respective IUPAC group suffixes in List II:

List I (Functional Group)List II (IUPAC Suffix)
A. \(-\mathrm{COOH}\)(i) -al
B. \(-\mathrm{CHO}\)(ii) -one
C. \(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)(iii) -nitrile
D. \(-\mathrm{CN}\)(iv) -oic acid

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In IUPAC nomenclature, the principal functional group in an organic compound determines the class suffix appended to the parent hydrocarbon name.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Functional Group
The carboxylic acid group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) takes the suffix "-oic acid", matching (iv). The aldehyde group (\(-\mathrm{CHO}\)) takes the suffix "-al", matching (i). The ketone group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)) takes the suffix "-one", matching (ii). The nitrile group (\(-\mathrm{CN}\)) takes the suffix "-nitrile", matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct matching is A-(iv), B-(i), C-(ii), D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
When present as subordinate functional groups in polyfunctional compounds, match the groups in List I with their IUPAC prefixes in List II:

List I (Subordinate Group)List II (IUPAC Prefix)
A. \(-\mathrm{CONH}_2\)(i) sulpho-
B. \(-\mathrm{COOR}\)(ii) carbamoyl-
C. \(-\mathrm{SO}_3\mathrm{H}\)(iii) halocarbonyl-
D. \(-\mathrm{COX}\)(iv) alkoxycarbonyl-

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In polyfunctional compounds, the group with the highest priority is given the principal suffix, while all remaining functional groups are treated as substituents and named using their IUPAC prefixes.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Group
The amide group (\(-\mathrm{CONH}_2\)) uses the prefix "carbamoyl-", matching (ii). The ester group (\(-\mathrm{COOR}\)) uses the prefix "alkoxycarbonyl-", matching (iv). The sulphonic acid group (\(-\mathrm{SO}_3\mathrm{H}\)) uses the prefix "sulpho-", matching (i). The acyl halide group (\(-\mathrm{COX}\)) uses the prefix "halocarbonyl-", matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match the cyclic organic compounds in List I with their structural classification in List II:

List I (Compound)List II (Classification)
A. Tetrahydrofuran(i) Non-benzenoid aromatic compound
B. Tropone(ii) Heterocyclic aromatic compound
C. Naphthalene(iii) Heterocyclic non-aromatic (alicyclic) compound
D. Thiophene(iv) Benzenoid aromatic compound

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Cyclic organic compounds are classified as alicyclic (non-aromatic rings) or aromatic (benzenoid or non-benzenoid), and either may be homocyclic (only carbon atoms in the ring) or heterocyclic (containing heteroatoms such as O, N, or S in the ring).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
Tetrahydrofuran is a saturated five-membered ring containing an oxygen atom; it is a heterocyclic non-aromatic (alicyclic) compound, matching (iii). Tropone has a seven-membered conjugated ring with a carbonyl group and is a non-benzenoid aromatic compound, matching (i). Naphthalene consists of two fused benzene rings and is a benzenoid aromatic compound, matching (iv). Thiophene is a five-membered aromatic ring containing a sulphur heteroatom, making it a heterocyclic aromatic compound, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q06 - Types of structural isomerism and examples

questiontext.text:
Match the pairs of organic compounds in List I with the type of structural isomerism they exhibit in List II:

List I (Pair of Compounds)List II (Type of Isomerism)
A. Pentane and 2-methylbutane(i) Functional group isomerism
B. Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol(ii) Chain isomerism
C. Propanal and propanone(iii) Metamerism
D. Methoxypropane and ethoxyethane(iv) Position isomerism

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Structural isomers share the same molecular formula but differ in atomic connectivity: chain isomers differ in carbon skeleton, position isomers differ in substituent/functional group location, functional group isomers have different functional groups, and metamers differ in alkyl chains on either side of a polyvalent functional group.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Pair
Pentane and 2-methylbutane both have the formula \(\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}\) with different carbon skeletons, illustrating chain isomerism, matching (ii). Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol both have \(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_8\mathrm{O}\) and differ only in the position of the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group, illustrating position isomerism, matching (iv). Propanal (aldehyde) and propanone (ketone) share \(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}\) with different functional groups, illustrating functional group isomerism, matching (i). Methoxypropane (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{OC}_3\mathrm{H}_7\)) and ethoxyethane (\(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{OC}_2\mathrm{H}_5\)) differ in alkyl chains flanking the ether oxygen, illustrating metamerism, matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match the electronic displacement effects in List I with their characteristic descriptions in List II:

List I (Effect)List II (Characteristic Description)
A. Inductive effect(i) Temporary transfer of \(\pi\)-electrons on demand of an attacking reagent
B. Electromeric effect(ii) Delocalisation of \(\mathrm{C-H}\) \(\sigma\)-electrons into an empty \(p\)-orbital or \(\pi\)-system
C. Resonance effect(iii) Permanent polarisation of \(\sigma\)-bonds due to electronegativity difference
D. Hyperconjugation(iv) Polarity produced by interaction of two \(\pi\)-bonds or a \(\pi\)-bond and lone pair

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electron displacements in organic molecules can be permanent (inductive, resonance, hyperconjugation) or temporary (electromeric), depending on whether they arise from substituents in the ground state or from an approaching reagent.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Effect
Inductive effect is the permanent polarisation of a \(\sigma\)-bond caused by the polarisation of an adjacent \(\sigma\)-bond due to electronegativity differences, matching (iii). Electromeric effect is a temporary, complete transfer of a shared pair of \(\pi\)-electrons to one atom of a multiple bond on the demand of an attacking reagent, matching (i). Resonance effect is the polarity produced by the interaction of two \(\pi\)-bonds or between a \(\pi\)-bond and a lone pair on an adjacent atom, matching (iv). Hyperconjugation is a permanent stabilising interaction involving delocalisation of \(\sigma\)-electrons of a \(\mathrm{C-H}\) bond into an adjacent empty \(p\)-orbital or unsaturated \(\pi\)-system, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match the substituents in the given molecules (List I) with the primary electronic effect they exert (List II):

List I (Substituent & Molecule)List II (Electronic Effect)
A. \(-\mathrm{NH}_2\) in aniline(i) \(-R\) effect (withdraws \(\pi\)-electrons from ring)
B. \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\) in nitrobenzene(ii) \(-I\) effect (withdraws \(\sigma\)-electrons)
C. \(-\mathrm{CH}_3\) in propene(iii) \(+R\) effect (donates lone pair into ring)
D. \(-\mathrm{Cl}\) in chloroethane(iv) Hyperconjugation (\(\sigma-\pi\) delocalisation)

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Substituents attached to conjugated rings, alkenes, or saturated chains alter electron distribution through resonance (\(+R\) or \(-R\)), inductive (\(-I\)), or hyperconjugation effects.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Substituent
In aniline, the \(-\mathrm{NH}_2\) group donates its nitrogen lone pair into the benzene ring, increasing electron density at ortho and para positions via the \(+R\) effect, matching (iii). In nitrobenzene, the \(-\mathrm{NO}_2\) group withdraws \(\pi\)-electrons from the benzene ring via the \(-R\) effect, matching (i). In propene, the methyl (\(-\mathrm{CH}_3\)) group stabilises the \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) double bond through \(\sigma-\pi\) delocalisation (hyperconjugation), matching (iv). In chloroethane, the electronegative \(-\mathrm{Cl}\) atom withdraws \(\sigma\)-electron density along the \(\mathrm{C-C}\) chain via the \(-I\) effect, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical species in List I with their correct classification as attacking reagents in List II:

List I (Species)List II (Classification)
A. \(\mathrm{BF}_3\)(i) Negatively charged nucleophile
B. \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N:}\)(ii) Neutral electrophile
C. \(\mathrm{HS}^-\)(iii) Positively charged electrophile
D. \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{C}^+=\mathrm{O}\)(iv) Neutral nucleophile

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleophiles are electron-rich species that donate an electron pair to an electron-deficient site, whereas electrophiles are electron-deficient species (with an incomplete octet or positive charge) that accept an electron pair.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Species
Boron trifluoride (\(\mathrm{BF}_3\)) is a neutral molecule in which boron has only six valence electrons (incomplete octet), so it acts as a neutral electrophile, matching (ii). Trimethylamine (\((\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\mathrm{N:}\)) is a neutral molecule with an unshared lone pair on nitrogen, so it acts as a neutral nucleophile, matching (iv). The hydrosulphide ion (\(\mathrm{HS}^-\)) carries a negative charge and lone pairs, making it a negatively charged nucleophile, matching (i). The acylium ion (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{C}^+=\mathrm{O}\)) has a positively charged, electron-deficient carbonyl carbon, making it a positively charged electrophile, matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Combining these gives A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

questiontext.text:
Match the purification techniques in List I with their underlying physical principles in List II:

List I (Purification Technique)List II (Principle)
A. Sublimation(i) Difference in solubilities of compound and impurities in a suitable solvent
B. Crystallisation(ii) Higher solubility of organic compound in an immiscible organic solvent than in water
C. Steam distillation(iii) Direct transition of solid to vapour state without passing through liquid state
D. Differential extraction(iv) Sum of vapour pressures of water and immiscible organic liquid equals atmospheric pressure

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Each purification technique exploits a distinct physical property difference between the desired organic compound and its impurities.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Technique
Sublimation separates sublimable solids from non-sublimable impurities based on direct solid-to-vapour transition without melting, matching (iii). Crystallisation purifies solids based on the difference in solubilities of the compound and impurities in a suitable solvent, matching (i). Steam distillation separates steam-volatile, water-immiscible liquids because the mixture boils when \(p_1 + p_2 = p_{\text{atm}}\), matching (iv). Differential extraction separates an organic compound from an aqueous medium using an immiscible organic solvent in which the compound is more soluble, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match the mixtures in List I with the most appropriate separation or purification method in List II:

List I (Mixture)List II (Purification Method)
A. Chloroform (b.p. \(334\text{ K}\)) and aniline (b.p. \(457\text{ K}\))(i) Fractional distillation
B. Glycerol from spent-lye in soap industry(ii) Distillation under reduced pressure
C. Different fractions of crude oil in petroleum industry(iii) Sublimation
D. Calcium sulphate and camphor(iv) Simple distillation

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Selecting the appropriate purification method depends on boiling point differences, thermal stability at the normal boiling point, and sublimability.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Mixture
Chloroform (\(334\text{ K}\)) and aniline (\(457\text{ K}\)) have a large boiling point difference (\(123\text{ K}\)) and are separated by simple distillation, matching (iv). Glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point, so it is separated from spent-lye by distillation under reduced pressure, matching (ii). Crude oil contains hydrocarbons with closely spaced boiling points that are separated by fractional distillation, matching (i). Camphor sublimes on heating whereas calcium sulphate is non-volatile, so they are separated by sublimation, matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(iv), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q12 - Qualitative analysis tests and characteristic colours

questiontext.text:
Match the element(s) detected in qualitative analysis of an organic compound (List I) with the corresponding test reagent and observation (List II):

List I (Element(s) Present)List II (Reagent & Observation)
A. Nitrogen only (Lassaigne's extract)(i) \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) ions; blood red colouration
B. Sulphur only (Lassaigne's extract)(ii) \(\mathrm{FeSO}_4\) and conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\); Prussian blue colour
C. Both N and S together (normal Na fusion)(iii) \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2\), \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\), and ammonium molybdate; yellow precipitate
D. Phosphorus(iv) Sodium nitroprusside; violet colouration

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In qualitative analysis, sodium fusion converts covalent N and S into ionic \(\mathrm{CN}^-\), \(\mathrm{S}^{2-}\), or \(\mathrm{SCN}^-\), while oxidation with \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) converts phosphorus into phosphate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Test
When only nitrogen is present, \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) reacts with \(\mathrm{FeSO}_4\) and conc. \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) to form \(\mathrm{Fe}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]_3\), giving a Prussian blue colour, matching (ii). When only sulphur is present, \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}\) reacts with sodium nitroprusside to form \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_5\mathrm{NOS}]^{4-}\), giving a violet colouration, matching (iv). When both nitrogen and sulphur are present, normal sodium fusion produces \(\mathrm{NaSCN}\), which reacts with \(\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}\) to give blood red \([\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{SCN})]^{2+}\), matching (i). Phosphorus is oxidised by \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{O}_2\) to phosphate, which on boiling with \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) and treating with ammonium molybdate yields a yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate, matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q13 - Silver nitrate test for halogens in Lassaigne's extract

questiontext.text:
In Lassaigne's test for halogens, match the halide species or procedural step in List I with the corresponding observation or purpose in List II:

List I (Halide / Step)List II (Observation / Purpose)
A. Chloride (\(\mathrm{Cl}^-\))(i) Yellowish precipitate, sparingly soluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\)
B. Bromide (\(\mathrm{Br}^-\))(ii) Boiling with conc. \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) to decompose \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) and \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}\)
C. Iodide (\(\mathrm{I}^-\))(iii) White precipitate, soluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\)
D. Pre-treatment when N or S is present(iv) Yellow precipitate, insoluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Silver halides (\(\mathrm{AgX}\)) have characteristic colours and solubilities in ammonium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\)). However, \(\mathrm{CN}^-\) and \(\mathrm{S}^{2-}\) ions also form precipitates with \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) and must be removed first.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Item
Chloride (\(\mathrm{Cl}^-\)) forms \(\mathrm{AgCl}\), a white precipitate soluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\), matching (iii). Bromide (\(\mathrm{Br}^-\)) forms \(\mathrm{AgBr}\), a yellowish precipitate sparingly soluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\), matching (i). Iodide (\(\mathrm{I}^-\)) forms \(\mathrm{AgI}\), a yellow precipitate insoluble in \(\mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{OH}\), matching (iv). Before adding \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\), the sodium fusion extract is boiled with conc. \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) to decompose any \(\mathrm{NaCN}\) or \(\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}\) that would otherwise interfere, matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Hence, the correct matching is A-(iii), B-(i), C-(iv), D-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q14 - Quantitative estimation methods and measured products

questiontext.text:
Match the element and estimation method in List I with the product weighed or measured in List II:

List I (Element & Method)List II (Measured / Weighed Product)
A. Carbon (Liebig's combustion)(i) Precipitate of \(\mathrm{AgX}\)
B. Nitrogen (Dumas method)(ii) \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) absorbed in \(\mathrm{KOH}\) solution
C. Halogens (Carius method)(iii) Precipitate of \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\)
D. Sulphur (Carius method)(iv) Volume of \(\mathrm{N}_2\) gas collected over \(\mathrm{KOH}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Quantitative elemental analysis converts each element in an organic compound into a stoichiometric, easily measurable gas or insoluble precipitate.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Method
In Liebig's combustion method, carbon is oxidised to \(\mathrm{CO}_2\), which is absorbed and weighed in a \(\mathrm{KOH}\) U-tube, matching (ii). In Dumas' method, nitrogen is converted to free \(\mathrm{N}_2\) gas and its volume is measured in a nitrometer over aqueous \(\mathrm{KOH}\), matching (iv). In the Carius method for halogens, heating with fuming \(\mathrm{HNO}_3\) and \(\mathrm{AgNO}_3\) precipitates silver halide (\(\mathrm{AgX}\)), matching (i). In the Carius method for sulphur, sulphur is oxidised to \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\) and precipitated as \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\) using \(\mathrm{BaCl}_2\), matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_Q15 - Percentage composition formulas in quantitative analysis

questiontext.text:
For an organic compound of mass \(m\text{ g}\), match the element being estimated in List I with the correct formula for its percentage composition in List II:

List I (Element & Product Mass)List II (Percentage Formula)
A. Carbon (mass of \(\mathrm{CO}_2 = m_2\text{ g}\))(i) \(\dfrac{2 \times m_1 \times 100}{18 \times m}\)
B. Hydrogen (mass of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} = m_1\text{ g}\))(ii) \(\dfrac{62 \times m_1 \times 100}{222 \times m}\)
C. Sulphur (mass of \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4 = m_1\text{ g}\))(iii) \(\dfrac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\)
D. Phosphorus (mass of \(\mathrm{Mg}_2\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_7 = m_1\text{ g}\))(iv) \(\dfrac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\)

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The mass percentage of an element is calculated from the mass fraction of that element in the isolated product multiplied by the product's mass, divided by the sample mass \(m\), and multiplied by \(100\).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Formula
For carbon, \(44\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) contains \(12\text{ g}\) of C, so \(\%\text{ C} = \frac{12 \times m_2 \times 100}{44 \times m}\), matching (iv). For hydrogen, \(18\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}\) contains \(2\text{ g}\) of H, so \(\%\text{ H} = \frac{2 \times m_1 \times 100}{18 \times m}\), matching (i). For sulphur, \(233\text{ g}\) of \(\mathrm{BaSO}_4\) contains \(32\text{ g}\) of S, so \(\%\text{ S} = \frac{32 \times m_1 \times 100}{233 \times m}\), matching (iii). For phosphorus estimated as \(\mathrm{Mg}_2\mathrm{P}_2\mathrm{O}_7\) (molar mass \(222\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)), each mole contains \(2 \times 31 = 62\text{ g}\) of P, so \(\%\text{ P} = \frac{62 \times m_1 \times 100}{222 \times m}\), matching (ii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the correct matching is A-(iv), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(ii).

questiontext.text:
Match the organic reactions in List I with their reaction types in List II:

List I (Reaction)List II (Reaction Type)
A. \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{HS}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{SH} + \mathrm{Br}^-\)(i) Elimination reaction
B. \((\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2 + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow (\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\mathrm{CCl}-\mathrm{CH}_3\)(ii) Nucleophilic substitution
C. \(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{Br} + \mathrm{HO}^- \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_2=\mathrm{CH}_2 + \mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O} + \mathrm{Br}^-\)(iii) Electrophilic substitution
D. \(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_6 + \mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{Cl} \xrightarrow{\text{anhyd. }\mathrm{AlCl}_3} \mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CH}_3 + \mathrm{HCl}\)(iv) Electrophilic addition

Choose the correct match from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Organic reactions are classified as substitution (one group replaces another), addition (two molecules combine across a multiple bond), or elimination (small molecule is removed to form a multiple bond), and further specified by the nature of the attacking reagent (nucleophile or electrophile).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
In the reaction of bromoethane with \(\mathrm{HS}^-\), the nucleophile \(\mathrm{HS}^-\) replaces \(\mathrm{Br}^-\), representing nucleophilic substitution, matching (ii). In the reaction of 2-methylpropene with \(\mathrm{HCl}\), \(\mathrm{H}^+\) adds first across the double bond followed by \(\mathrm{Cl}^-\), representing electrophilic addition, matching (iv). In the reaction of bromoethane with \(\mathrm{HO}^-\) forming ethene, \(\mathrm{HBr}\) is eliminated to create a \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) double bond, representing an elimination reaction, matching (i). In the Friedel-Crafts methylation of benzene, the electrophile \(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\) substitutes a ring hydrogen, representing electrophilic substitution, matching (iii).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Thus, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii).
